subject: Request: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback for FinSecure
messages:
From: Anna Muller <procurement@finsecure.eu>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Pedro Silva <psilva@finsecure.eu>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback for FinSecure

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal have one blocking requirement before we can sign: FinSecure needs all inference for our account to be bound to an EU-resident model variant (they named the variant "redwood-eu-fin-1") and we explicitly cannot allow automatic fallback to any non-EU or lower-cost variant under any capacity shortage.

Summary of asks:
- Region lock: route all requests for account FinSecure to the EU region (data residency + audit).
- Forced model selection: pin to redwood-eu-fin-1; no automatic fallback allowed.
- Auditability: request logs showing per-request model variant and routing decisions for audit (retention: 7 years).
- SLA/credits: because this reduces your failover options, we expect commensurate SLA language — see attached redlines.

I've attached the SLA redlines (PDF). Please confirm feasibility, operational impact, and an expected timeline to provide formal confirmation to our legal team. We need a signed contract by 2027-08-20 to meet our board timeline.

Best,
Anna Muller
Procurement Lead, FinSecure

Attachment: FinSecure_SLA_redlines.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Muller <procurement@finsecure.eu>, Pedro Silva <psilva@finsecure.eu>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback for FinSecure

Thanks Anna — forwarding internally to evaluate. Quick notes up front: this is a hard constraint and will change our available recovery/fallback options. Product and Ops: can you assess shipping constraints and a proposed rollout/mitigation plan? Legal: please advise on whether the SLA redlines as-is are acceptable or need counter proposals.

I've also attached a small sizer matrix to help evaluate variants and capacity: model-variant-matrix.csv (internal).

Initial questions for product/ops:
- Is it possible to create a customer-specific route that forbids any fallback to non-EU variants (baked into routing config)?
- If redwood-eu-fin-1 is unavailable, do we fail requests outright or queue/retry? (Customer insists on no fallback, but we need clarity on behavior under infrastructure failure.)
- What is the expected incremental cost (per-token) for pinned EU-only capacity if we reserve capacity vs. relying on multi-tenant pooled capacity?

Please respond with owner for each bullet and a rough ETA. I'll coordinate with Anna and Pedro after we have internal alignment.

—Markus
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: model-variant-matrix.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Muller <procurement@finsecure.eu>, Pedro Silva <psilva@finsecure.eu>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:26:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback for FinSecure

Markus / team,

Technical assessment (high level):
1) Route policy: We can implement an account-scoped routing policy that pins FinSecure to the redwood-eu-fin-1 model and restricts routing to EU regions only. That can be enforced at the Smart Router layer and surfaced in the Console as a "Hard Lock".

2) Fallback behavior: We currently have two options:
   - Fail fast: if the pinned variant is unavailable, return a 5xx (or a customer-configured error) — this matches FinSecure's "no fallback" ask.
   - Soft-queue: automatically retry for a short window while the platform attempts to recover the variant. This still keeps the model pinned but improves availability at the risk of longer latency.

Customer is explicit about "no fallback to non-EU or lower-cost models." If they truly mean "no fallback of any kind," we should clarify whether short retries to the same EU variant are acceptable (I recommend allowing limited retries to the same variant but not fallback to any alternative).

3) Capacity and cost: Pinning to a single EU variant without fallback increases the tail-cost. Two recommended approaches:
   - Dedicated capacity reservation (recommended for production-critical FinSecure workloads).
   - Priority burst on pooled capacity with strict routing and SLA credits baked in (less expensive but operationally riskier).

4) Audit logs: We can emit per-request routing metadata (model_variant, region, timestamp) and surface it via a secure S3/GCS export or a log API. Retention for 7 years is doable with an archive tier, but it will be an additional storage/cost line item.

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Product (me): prepare config spec and Console UI change ticket for a "EU hard-lock + no-fallback mode" (ETA: 6 business days for spec, 14 business days for an initial behind-feature rollout).
- Ops (Mina): sizing for dedicated capacity vs. pooled burst and cost delta (ETA: 3 business days).
- Policy/Legal (Priyom & Lauren): review SLA redlines and define language for availability/credits if we will "fail fast" (ETA: 4 business days).

I'll draft the spec and put it in the shared Drive; Markus, please let me know if we should prioritize a Console toggle (fast) vs. programmatic-only routing (safer for first release).

-Karthik
Group PM, Serving Runtime

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Muller <procurement@finsecure.eu>, Pedro Silva <psilva@finsecure.eu>, FinSecure Legal <legal@finsecure.eu>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 15:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: EU-only model enforcement + no-fallback for FinSecure

Markus/Karthik/Mina/Priyom — thanks for the quick assessment. Legal review notes below.

- SLA redlines: we can accept redlines that require an EU-only, pinned variant, but we need explicit contract language that describes failure modes. If the customer insists on "no fallback of any kind," the contract must reflect that we will return errors during infrastructure outages and that certain availability targets will not apply (or will carry a different credits formula). I propose two options for the contract:
  1) No-fallback (Fail-fast): explicit clause that we will not redirect traffic to other variants; availability credits are capped to X% and do not apply for third-party infra outages.
  2) EU-pinned with retries: allow short retry windows to the same EU variant; availability credits remain largely intact.

- Audit log retention: 7-year retention is legally fine but we must note the cost and include it as a billable line item. Also need to confirm export controls and encryption-at-rest (KMS).

- Compliance asks: FinSecure requires SOC2 + customer-specific attestations. We have SOC2 reports; for extra attestation language we'll need an addendum.

Immediate ask to Sales (Markus): get customer to confirm which contract option they prefer (1 or 2). If they pick option 1 (strict fail-fast), ask them to accept the counter-SLA language in the attached redlines. If they pick option 2, product can proceed with the retry-safe implementation.

I'm happy to join a call with FinSecure legal if needed. Suggest the following owners & timeline:
- Product (Karthik): spec and Console toggle draft (ETA 6 business days).
- Ops (Mina): capacity delta and cost (ETA 3 business days).
- Legal (Lauren & Priyom): final SLA language and addendum draft (ETA 4 business days).
- Sales (Markus): confirm customer's contract option and expected sign date (target: 2027-08-20).

Markus — if you can get a short note from FinSecure saying which option they want, we can fast-track the work.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
